what: a manticore, the man-eater of Persian legend: a monster with the head of a human man on the body of a dark red-brown lion, one animal on four legs, painted seriously as a real and dangerous beast. In place of a lion's head it has a man's head, the size of a lion's head: the fierce face of an ancient Persian king looking straight at the viewer, with smooth bare pale tan human skin on the forehead, cheeks and nose, a high human forehead, a straight narrow human nose, human lips, human ears, and two cold pale human eyes under heavy black brows. A plain narrow gold band lies across his forehead. He has thick black curled human hair hanging to the shoulders and a long, square-cut, tightly curled black human beard, and no mane. His human mouth is stretched very wide open, crowded with rows of sharp white teeth. Behind the head it is all animal: the thick neck, deep chest, long lean body, four legs and great clawed paws of a real lion, covered all over in short thick dark red-brown fur the colour of old mahogany, nearly black along the spine and under the belly. The lion has no lion's tail: its tail is the tail of a giant black scorpion, held high, thick, jointed and armoured in glossy black plates, curving up and forward over its back, and the tail swells at its end into a fat glossy black bulb with one long curved needle-point.
colours: short dark red-brown fur the colour of old mahogany on the body and legs, nearly black along the spine and under the belly, a smooth pale tan human face, black curled human hair and a long black beard, a narrow gold brow band, a glossy black jointed scorpion tail and sting, white teeth, black claws.
wears: It is a beast and wears nothing.
holds: It is a beast on four legs and holds nothing.
pose: Seen from the side, its body faces left on four legs: all four paws are on the ground, front end crouched low and hindquarters high, ready to spring, its black scorpion tail arched up over its back with the sting aimed forward; the man's head is raised and turned full-face to the viewer, so the whole bare human face, the gold brow band and the black beard show, roaring with the mouth wide open.
must_show: a lion's furred body on four legs, rust-red
a human man's head the size of a lion's: bare pale tan skin, human nose, black hair and a long black beard
a wide mouth with rows of sharp teeth
a thick black jointed scorpion tail with a bulb and needle sting arched over the back
younger and plainer than the elder manticore: black hair, no grey, no knob of spines
must_not_show: head as big as the body

what: a necromancer's apprentice: a thin, pale, living young man, hollow-cheeked and unshaven, with lank black hair to his jaw, dark rings under his eyes and an eager, reckless stare. He has realistic adult proportions: a small head, long limbs, about eight heads tall.
colours: pale sallow living skin, lank black hair, a plain dark charcoal-grey wool robe with a frayed hem, a brown rope belt, a brown leather satchel, a plain dark brown wooden staff with one small ivory bird skull, a sickly yellow-green flame.
wears: He wears a plain, cheap, dark charcoal-grey wool robe with long sleeves and a frayed muddy hem, tied with a rope belt, a worn leather satchel at his hip and scuffed brown boots. No hood, bare head. No jewellery.
holds: He holds exactly one plain wooden staff in his left hand, gripped at the middle: a thick, straight, dark brown pole as tall as his shoulder with one small ivory bird skull tied to its top with cord. His right hand is empty and thrust forward, open, with one round ball of sickly yellow-green flame as big as his fist burning in the palm, touching the hand. He holds nothing else.
pose: On two legs, he lunges forward with his weight on his front foot and his robe swinging, his right arm thrust straight out ahead hurling the ball of flame from his open palm, the staff held back and upright in his left hand, his mouth open shouting a spell.
must_show: a thin pale living young man in a plain dark grey robe, bare-headed
one plain wooden staff with a small bird skull on top
a ball of sickly yellow-green flame in the open right palm
poor and plain: a beginner, no finery

what: a pale master: a necromancer who has rebuilt his own body from grave goods and is now more corpse than man. He is tall, gaunt and bald, with dead flesh, chalk-white and corpse-grey, never the colour of living flesh, on the scalp, face, neck and arms alike; sunken cheeks, a lipless thin mouth, and two blank milk-white eyes that do not blink. Thick black stitches run across his scalp and round his neck. His right forearm and hand are plainly not his own: from a ring of thick black stitches at the elbow down, that arm is a different dead man's, darker, withered, leather-brown, with long bony fingers. Strapped over his chest outside his robe is a cage of big old off-white human rib bones, the colour of dirty ivory, a breastplate of borrowed ribs. He has realistic adult proportions: a small head, long limbs, about eight heads tall.
colours: chalk-white and corpse-grey dead skin, one withered leather-brown grafted forearm and hand, thick black stitches, a long black robe with dull bone-grey edges, a breastplate of off-white dirty-ivory rib bones, nearly white, on black leather straps, blank milk-white eyes, one sickly yellow-green flame.
wears: He wears a long black sleeveless robe that falls from the neck to the ground, belted with a black leather strap, and over it the breastplate of big off-white rib bones strapped across his chest. His arms are bare to show the stitches. No hood, bare bald head. No crown.
holds: His hands are empty. His withered brown right hand reaches forward, open, with the long fingers spread to touch, and a small sickly yellow-green flame burns close round its fingertips, touching the hand. His pale left hand is held open at his side. He has no staff and no weapon.
pose: On two legs, he strides forward in a long step with his weight on his front foot and his body leaning in, his withered brown right arm stretched straight out ahead to lay its touch on the viewer, his pale left arm swept back, his bald head lowered and his blank white eyes fixed ahead, his black robe swinging behind.
must_show: a tall gaunt bald dead man, chalk-white and corpse-grey skin, head included
thick black stitches on the scalp, neck and arm
one grafted forearm and hand of a different, darker brown colour
a breastplate of big rib bones strapped over a black robe
empty hands, a small yellow-green flame at the reaching fingertips
plainly the master: dead, grafted and armoured in bone, unlike the living apprentice

what: a hollow one: the walking corpse of a person who sold their soul, gaunt as famine, dead flesh the colour of old putty, a cold chalk-grey with a faint grey-green tinge that no living person has, on the face, neck, arms, hands and legs alike. It has a long bald head with sunken temples, two empty black eye sockets, and a lower jaw dropped far open in an endless shriek, the mouth a tall black oval. In the middle of its chest, where the heart was, is the mark of the bargain: one large, perfectly round, pitch-black hole as wide as its two fists, clean-edged, empty and dark, with a thin rim of pale ash-grey round it. Its arms are long and thin, and each hand has five long thin bony fingers spread wide apart like the ribs of a fan. It has the realistic proportions of a starved adult: a small head, long limbs, about eight heads tall.
colours: cold chalk-grey dead skin with a faint grey-green tinge, like old putty, the same on every bare part, black eye sockets, a black open mouth, one round pitch-black hole in the chest, a ragged dull mud-brown burial shroud.
wears: It wears the rags of a dull mud-brown burial shroud, wound round its hips and legs to the shins and hanging in tatters from one shoulder, torn open over the chest so the round black hole shows. Its feet are bare.
holds: Its hands are empty: two long bony grey hands, open, the fingers hooked to grasp, holding nothing.
pose: On two legs, it lurches forward with its weight on its front foot and its knees bent, both long arms stretched out ahead with the fingers hooked to seize, its head thrown back and its jaw gaping wide in a shriek, the shroud tatters trailing behind.
must_show: a gaunt corpse-grey dead figure, head and hands the same grey
one large round pitch-black hole in the middle of the chest
jaw gaping in a shriek, empty black eye sockets
both empty hands reaching to grasp
brown shroud rags

what: a medusa: one of the lesser gorgons, a daughter of Medusa who hunts in the dark among her statues. She is a tall, graceful, beautiful and terrible young woman standing on two legs, with exactly two arms, with skin that is plainly not a living colour: pale ash-grey with a faint scaly sheen, on the face, neck, arms and hands alike. Her face is beautiful, young, cold and cruel: smooth unlined ash-grey skin, high cheekbones, a straight nose, full dark lips parted to show two long white snake fangs, arched black brows, and two wide eyes that are blank glowing yellow with no pupils. She has no hair: growing from her whole scalp in its place are seven very thick living snakes, each as thick as her arm, glossy black vipers with pale yellow bellies and large wedge-shaped heads, rearing up and outward in different directions with their white mouths gaping wide. Her forearms and the backs of her hands are covered in black snake scales, and her fingers end in long black claws. She has realistic adult proportions: a small head, long limbs, about eight heads tall.
colours: pale ash-grey skin on face, arms and hands, thick glossy black snakes with pale yellow bellies and white mouths, blank glowing yellow eyes, a long plain undyed cream linen Greek dress, a tarnished bronze belt and two bronze shoulder pins, a dull grey shawl, black scaled forearms and black claws.
wears: She wears a long, plain, undyed cream linen Greek dress that covers her from the shoulders to the ankles, pinned at each shoulder with a bronze pin and belted with a tarnished bronze belt, and a ragged dull grey shawl over her elbows; leather sandals. No crown, no armour, no jewels.
holds: Her hands are empty: two clawed hands holding nothing. She has no weapon and no shield.
pose: On two legs, she lunges to the left with her weight on her front foot under the long dress, her body leaning in, her left hand raised beside her face with the claws spread and her right arm stretched out ahead with the claws spread, her head thrust forward, her yellow eyes glaring straight at the viewer, every snake of her hair rearing outward and hissing.
must_show: a grey-skinned woman with a head of very thick black snakes in place of hair, readable as snakes in the small sprite
a beautiful, cold young face
a plain long cream Greek dress, fully clothed
scaled forearms and empty clawed hands
plainer than Medusa herself: no gold diadem, no crimson gown, no bronze armour
must_not_show: snake tail for a lower body

what: a mimic: a small monster in the shape of a plain, cheap, battered wooden storage chest, caught at the moment it bites. It is one small box of rough grey-brown pine planks with a flat lid, two rusty iron strap hinges, a rusty iron hasp and a loop of old rope for a handle at each end, with no metal bands and no ornament. The flat lid has swung half open, and the chest is a pair of jaws: a row of short, thick, uneven yellowed fangs runs along the rim of the lid and along the rim of the box, and the inside is very dark wet flesh, a brown so dark it is nearly black. Between the lid and the box stretch a dozen thick strings of dull grey-white glue, the colour of old candle wax, sagging, and fat beads of the same dull grey-white glue ooze down the front planks. The wood is scarred, stained and weathered. It has no eyes and no tongue.
colours: rough grey-brown weathered pine planks, dark brown rusty iron hinges the colour of an old nail, frayed tan rope handles, yellowed ivory fangs, a very dark brown wet inside that is nearly black, thick dull grey-white glue strands and beads the colour of old candle wax.
wears: It wears nothing.
holds: It holds nothing.
pose: Seen from the front and a little to one side: the chest lurches up and to the left, tilted on one corner, its flat fanged lid snapping open with the grey-white glue strings stretching between the two rows of fangs, glue beading on its front. It has nothing under it.
must_show: a small plain plank chest with rope handles that is a monster
the lid and the box rim lined with short thick fangs
thick amber glue strands stretched across the open jaws and beading on the wood
weathered, stained painted wood, not a cartoon chest
plainer and smaller than the lurking horror: no iron bands, no arm, no tongue

what: a gilded mimic: an ancient, enormous mimic that disguises itself as a king's treasure, the richest kin of the plain plank-chest mimic and plainly the same kind, caught at the moment it stops pretending, painted seriously with weight and grime. It is one great heavy treasure chest of old gold, its sides covered in raised scrollwork, with a high rounded lid and heavy corner plates, heaped to the brim with old gold coins. The gold is ancient and dull: deep brown-gold like tarnished brass, dented and grimy, with dark brown shadows in every hollow, never bright or new. The lid is thrown wide open, and the chest is a pair of jaws: along the whole rim of the lid and the whole rim of the box runs a crowded row of very long, thick, uneven yellowed bone fangs, real teeth, and a second shorter row stands behind the first. Under the coins the inside is wet dark flesh, almost black. Between the lid and the box stretch a dozen thick sagging strings of pale amber glue. Out of the open jaws, over the front rim, hangs one thick tapering tongue of wet flesh, smooth, slick and glistening, dark maroon-brown, as thick as the lid at its root and narrowing to a blunt tip; it sags down the front of the chest and its tip lifts and reaches out to the left. A few gold coins are stuck flat to the wet tongue. It has no eyes.
colours: deep old brown-gold the colour of tarnished brass on the chest and coins, with dark brown shadows; long yellowed ivory fangs; a dark brown-black wet inside; pale amber-yellow glue strands; one smooth wet dark maroon-brown tongue with a few dull gold coins stuck to it.
wears: It wears nothing.
holds: It holds nothing.
pose: Seen from the front and a little to one side: the great gold chest lurches up and to the left, tilted on one corner, its fanged lid gaping wide with the amber glue strings stretching between the two rows of fangs, coins sliding over its front rim, the heavy coin-crusted tongue pushing straight out low to the left. The chest is one compact mass with a clean lower edge and nothing under it.
must_show: an ornate old-gold treasure chest that is a monster, heaped with coins
the open lid and the box rim lined with long yellowed bone fangs, readable in the small sprite
one thick smooth wet dark tongue hanging out of the jaws and reaching left, not curled in a spiral
dull tarnished gold with dark shadows: grim, not a shiny toy
the richest mimic: gold all over, where the plain mimic is bare planks
must_not_show: coins scattered loose across the floor

what: Asterion, the Minotaur of the Labyrinth of Crete, son of a queen and the white bull of the sea god: a huge, immensely broad, heavily muscled man standing upright on two human legs, with the head of a great bull. He is far grander than a common minotaur. His bull's head, thick neck, shoulders, chest, belly and arms are covered in short pure white bull's hide, scarred with old grey scars; the head has a broad white muzzle with a dark grey nose, small furious dark red eyes, and two very long, thick, ivory-white horns that sweep out and forward; the horns are bone-white for most of their length, and only the last hand's length of each sharp tip is sheathed in a cap of bright gold. He has the realistic proportions of a giant adult man, with the bull's head no larger than his chest.
colours: short pure white bull's hide on the head, chest and arms with pale grey shadows and grey scars, a dark grey muzzle, dark red eyes, long ivory-white horns with small bright gold caps on the tips only, a broad gold and dark red royal collar, a long dark crimson war-kilt with a gold key-pattern border, a wide bronze belt, bronze wrist shackles with short broken bronze chains.
wears: He wears the regalia of a prince of Crete: a broad royal collar of gold plates and dark red stones across his chest and shoulders, a wide bronze belt, and a long dark crimson war-kilt with a gold key-pattern border that hangs to his knees. On each wrist is a thick bronze shackle with a short broken length of heavy bronze chain, three big links, hanging from it. His feet are bare.
holds: His hands are empty: two enormous clenched fists holding nothing. He has no axe and no weapon.
pose: Seen from the side and a little from the front, facing left, on two legs: he is charging, running at full tilt on his two human legs with his body pitched far forward from the hips, his head down so the two long horns point straight ahead to the left to gore, one knee driving up high and the back leg stretched out behind, one fist punched forward and the other swung back, the broken chains flying from his wrists, the crimson kilt streaming back, his mouth open in a bellow.
must_show: a massive upright man with a white bull's head, two legs
white hide on the head, chest and arms
very long ivory horns with gold tips, lowered to gore, in a running charge on two legs
a gold royal collar and a crimson kilt with a gold border
bronze shackles with broken chains on both wrists
empty fists
plainly a boss: grander than the plain brown minotaur
must_not_show: tan human skin on the chest
long chains wrapped round the body

what: a brown mold: a cold, foul dungeon growth, painted seriously as real rot with depth and grime. It is one low, lumpy, heaped clump of dark fuzzy mould, wider than it is tall, one thick, ragged, uneven crust of mould, heaped, wrinkled and folded on itself in a dozen irregular lumps and ridges of different sizes, no two alike, its whole surface matted with short dense mould fuzz and dusted with paler powder on the ridges, with deep black cracks and hollows between the lumps and a ragged, torn, creeping edge. It drinks the warmth out of the air: its whole outer edge is crusted with hard white frost, and a row of short thick white icicles hangs from its ragged lower edge on the left side. Half buried in the middle of the clump is one burnt-out wooden torch, a short black charred stick, with mould grown over it.
colours: dark chocolate-brown and dull umber fuzzy mould with paler tan dust on the ridges, black hollows, hard white frost and white icicles along the edges, one black charred torch stick.
wears: It wears nothing.
holds: It holds nothing.
pose: The clump swells and creeps to the left, heaped highest at the right, its ragged left edge creeping forward in two or three uneven tongues rimmed with frost and icicles. It is one compact lump with a clean lower edge.
must_show: a low, ragged, lumpy crust of dark brown fuzzy mould with dark cracks, not leaves and not neat balls
white frost and short icicles on its edges
foul, grimy painted growth with depth
no face and no limbs

what: a yellow mold: a dry, poisonous dungeon growth, painted seriously as real rot with depth and grime. It is one low, lumpy, heaped clump of dry mould, wider than it is tall: one thick, ragged, uneven crust, heaped, wrinkled and folded on itself in a dozen irregular lumps and ridges of different sizes, no two alike, its whole surface dry, cracked and powdery, with deep dark brown cracks and hollows between the lumps and a ragged, torn, creeping edge. The crust is a dull dirty yellow-brown, the colour of dry mustard powder mixed with dust, with pale dry sulphur-yellow powder dusted only along the tops of the ridges. Sticking out of the clump at angles are one broken rotten grey plank and the ends of two long old bones, grey-brown as if dug from a grave, with mould creeping up them. One lump at the top has burst open in a dark ragged hole, and from the hole one small tight puff of pale yellow dust shoots upward, joined to the hole.
colours: dull dirty yellow-brown and khaki dry powdery mould, pale sulphur-yellow dust only on the ridges, dark brown cracks and hollows, one dark grey rotten plank, two grey-brown old bones, one small puff of pale yellow dust.
wears: It wears nothing.
holds: It holds nothing.
pose: The clump swells and creeps to the left, heaped highest at the right, its ragged left edge creeping forward in two or three uneven tongues, the plank and the bone ends jutting from its back, the small puff of yellow dust bursting up and to the left from its top. It is one compact lump with a clean lower edge.
must_show: a low, ragged, lumpy crust of dry, cracked, powdery mould, not nuggets and not neat balls
dull dirty yellow-brown with sulphur dust on the ridges: never gold, never bright
a rotten plank and old bone ends sticking out
one small puff of yellow spore dust joined to the top
no face and no limbs
must_not_show: cloud of spores round the body

what: a myconid worker: a fungus that walks, painted seriously as rotting woodland growth come alive, eerie and never cute. It is short, squat and stooped. Its body is one thick, lumpy, fibrous mushroom stalk, pale and dirt-stained, with ragged torn skin hanging from it in strips. In place of a head it has one broad, drooping, misshapen mushroom cap with a ragged split edge and dark gills underneath, sagging low over the top of the stalk. It has no face: under the rim of the cap there is only deep black shadow. Two long thin arms of twisted pale root-fibre hang nearly to the ground, each ending in three long root fingers. It walks on two short thick legs of the same fibrous stalk that end in spreading root-toes. Small pale bracket fungi grow on its back.
colours: a dull grey-brown cap with darker umber blotches and a pale tan torn edge, dark brown gills, a pale bone-cream stalk body stained with dark brown dirt, pale grey root-fibre arms, one small puff of dull ochre-yellow spores.
wears: It is a fungus and wears nothing.
holds: Its hands are empty: two long three-fingered root hands holding nothing.
pose: On two short legs, it shambles forward stooped, with its weight on its front foot, one long root arm reaching out ahead with the fingers spread and the other dragging behind, its heavy cap tilted down, and from the top of the cap one small tight puff of ochre-yellow spores shoots upward, joined to the cap.
must_show: a squat stooped walking fungus with one drooping grey-brown cap for a head
no face: only black shadow under the cap
long root-fibre arms with three fingers, empty
a small puff of ochre spores joined to the cap
eerie, weathered, painted growth, not a cartoon mushroom person
must_not_show: cloud of spores round the body

what: a myconid sovereign: the ancient mind of a whole fungus cavern, a tall, gaunt, towering fungus that walks upright, painted seriously as old rotting growth, dreadful and never cute. Its body is one tall, thick, solid, gnarled mushroom stalk, pale and deeply furrowed from top to bottom, whole and unbroken, with a few clusters of small dark toadstools sprouting from its shoulders. In place of a head it has a huge, heavy, dark mushroom cap, broad as its shoulders and ragged at the rim, and on top of that cap a ring of tall narrow fungus spires stands upright. Under the rim of the cap, in deep black shadow, burn two narrow slanted glowing amber slits with no pupils. From its shoulders to the ground, down its back and both sides, hangs a long, heavy, thick mantle of pale root-threads, a dense curtain of hanging fibres as full as a fur cloak, far wider than its body. Its two arms are long and thick, of twisted root-fibre, each ending in a heavy knotted fist of roots. It walks on two thick stalk legs.
colours: a dark umber-brown and black-brown cap with a ring of dull ochre spires on top and pale cream gills beneath, a pale ash-grey furrowed stalk body, small dark umber toadstools on the shoulders, a pale bone-cream mantle of root-threads, two narrow amber eye slits, one small puff of dull ochre-yellow spores.
wears: It is a fungus and wears nothing but its own growth: the ring of spires on its cap and the hanging mantle of root-threads are part of it.
holds: Its hands are empty: two heavy knotted root fists holding nothing. It has no staff.
pose: On two legs, it strides forward with its weight on its front foot and its body leaning in, its right fist raised high above its cap ready to slam down, its left arm stretched out ahead with the root fingers spread, the mantle of root-threads swinging behind, and from the palm of its left hand one small tight puff of ochre-yellow spores bursts forward, touching the hand.
must_show: a tall gaunt walking fungus with a huge dark cap
a ring of tall fungus spires standing on the cap
no face: only shadow under the cap
a long hanging mantle of pale root-threads
a solid pale stalk body with no ribs or bones
empty root fists, one raised to slam
plainly the ruler: tall, spired and mantled where the worker is squat and bare
must_not_show: cloud of spores round the body

what: an ogre: the man-eating monster of the old fairy tales, painted seriously as a real and dangerous brute. It has a massive, fat, hunched body standing upright on two thick bowed legs, neckless, with slab shoulders, one great round sagging belly that hangs over its kilt, and long heavy arms, thicker than its legs, that hang to its knees and end in huge hands with thick black claws. It is a monster, not a man, and it is fat and heavy, not muscled: its whole body is covered in thick, rough, cracked, wrinkled hide, dull grey-brown, the colour of dried mud, on the scalp, face, chest, belly, arms and legs alike, darker in the creases, with a ridge of coarse black bristles along the shoulders and down the forearms. Its one head is sunk between the shoulders: small and bald with a broad, fleshy, living face: heavy jowls, a wide flat snout with two flared nostrils, thick dark lips, small mean dull-yellow eyes under a heavy overhanging brow, ragged torn pointed ears, and a huge heavy lower jaw, wider than the skull, jutting far out, with two thick ivory tusks as long as fingers rising from it past the snout. It has the build of a huge fat brute with a small head.
colours: dull grey-brown cracked hide the colour of dried mud on every part, darker grey in the creases, coarse black bristles, ivory tusks, dull yellow eyes, black claws, a dark brown shaggy hide kilt, a necklace of big grey-white bones, a dark brown wooden club.
wears: He wears only a ragged kilt of dark brown shaggy animal hide held up by a rope, and a string of big grey-white bones round his neck. His chest, belly and feet are bare hide.
holds: He holds exactly one club in his right hand, raised: one straight length of dark wood as long as his arm, narrow at the grip and swelling to a thick knobbly end, with nothing fixed to it. His left hand is empty, a huge open clawed hand. He holds nothing else.
pose: On two legs, he lumbers forward hunched with his weight on his front foot, his right arm raised high and back with the club ready to smash down, his left hand reaching out ahead to grab, his tusked jaw open in a roar.
must_show: a huge fat hunched monster with dull grey-brown hide on every part: plainly not a man
a great sagging belly, no stomach muscles
a small bald fleshy head with a jutting jaw, two big tusks and small eyes
exactly one head
one plain knobbly wooden club raised in the right hand, an empty clawed left hand
a ragged hide kilt and bone necklace, nothing else

what: a two-headed ogre, painted seriously as a real and dangerous brute: one body with two heads. It has a massive, fat, hunched body standing upright on two thick bowed legs, neckless, with slab shoulders, one great round sagging belly that hangs over its kilt, and long heavy arms, thicker than its legs, that hang to its knees and end in huge hands with thick black claws. It is a monster, not a man, and it is fat and heavy, not muscled: its whole body is covered in thick, rough, cracked, wrinkled hide, dull grey-brown, the colour of dried mud, on the scalp, face, chest, belly, arms and legs alike, darker in the creases, with a ridge of coarse black bristles along the shoulders and down the forearms. The two heads sit side by side on its one wide pair of shoulders, each on its own short thick neck, the two necks leaning apart like the arms of a letter V, so there is a gap of empty air between the heads. Each head is small and bald with a broad, fleshy, living face: heavy jowls, a wide flat snout with two flared nostrils, thick dark lips, small mean dull-yellow eyes under a heavy overhanging brow, ragged torn pointed ears, and a huge heavy lower jaw, wider than the skull, jutting far out, with two thick ivory tusks as long as fingers rising from it past the snout. The left head is roaring with its jaw wide open and looks ahead to the left; the right head scowls with its jaw shut and looks the other way, to the right, keeping watch.
colours: dull grey-brown cracked hide the colour of dried mud on every part and on both heads, darker grey in the creases, coarse black bristles, ivory tusks, dull yellow eyes, black claws, a dark brown shaggy hide kilt, one broad black leather strap with dull iron studs, two dark brown wooden clubs.
wears: It wears a ragged kilt of dark brown shaggy animal hide and one broad black leather strap with iron studs slung across its chest from one shoulder. Its belly and feet are bare hide.
holds: It holds exactly two clubs, one in each hand: each club is one short, very thick length of dark wood, no longer than its forearm, narrow at the grip where the fist closes round it and swelling to a fat knobbly end as thick as its own head, with nothing fixed to it. Each hand grips one club and only one, by the narrow end. The right hand's club is raised high above the heads; the left hand's club is held out low to the left side, its fat end pointing down. The two clubs are far apart and do not touch.
pose: On two legs, it stamps forward hunched with its weight on its front foot and its arms spread wide, the right club raised high to smash down and the left club swung out low and wide, the left head roaring ahead and the right head turned away scowling over the other shoulder.
must_show: one huge fat hunched monster body with dull grey-brown hide: plainly not a man
two small bald fleshy tusked heads side by side on separate necks, living faces
the two heads looking in different directions
a short fat wooden club in each hand, two clubs
plainly the same kind as the ogre, with a second head, a second club and a studded strap
must_not_show: heads stacked one above the other

what: a gray ooze: a foul dungeon slime that passes for a patch of wet stone until it strikes, painted with depth, weight and grime. It is one single thick mass of heavy, wet, cloudy slime, the colour of wet slate. It is one low rounded mound, soft all over, twice as wide as it is tall, heaped in three or four heavy sagging rolls, and its front edge lifts in one thick rounded lip that curls up and over, no higher than the mound itself, blunt and swollen, with no features. Its skin is dull and murky, not clear: mottled with darker streaks, pitted, slick with wet grey highlights, with a few thick drips sagging from the underside of the curled lip. Stuck in the top of the mound, half eaten away, is one piece of rusted iron mail, a ragged scrap of chain links, pitted and crumbling.
colours: dark slate-grey and neutral stone-grey murky slime with charcoal streaks and pale grey wet highlights, a warm neutral grey with no blue tint, one very dark brown rusted scrap of chain mail the colour of an old iron nail.
wears: It wears nothing.
holds: It holds nothing.
pose: The mound heaves and rolls to the left, heaped highest at the right, its front edge at the left lifting in one thick rounded lip that curls up and over, about to slap down, a few thick drips hanging from the lip. It is one joined compact mass, twice as wide as tall, with a clean lower edge.

Out of the slime on its back and right side grow about eight large, long, six-sided spikes of quartz crystal, of different sizes, sharp-tipped, standing up and leaning backward at different angles, each one rooted in the soft slime, which bulges up a little round its base. holds: He holds exactly one greatcleaver in both hands: a butcher's cleaver made huge, a very broad, flat, heavy rectangular steel blade as long as his leg and as wide as his forearm is long, with a straight edge, a squared-off end, a round hole near its top corner, and a long dark two-handed grip. Both of his fists are clenched round the grip close together, one above the other, in front of his right shoulder at chest height, and the great blade rises straight up out of the top fist above that shoulder, plainly joined to the grip. He holds nothing else, and nothing hangs from his belt.
pose: On two legs, he lunges forward hunched with his weight on his front foot and his head lowered so the great tusks point ahead, the greatcleaver swung up and back over his right shoulder in both hands ready to hew down, the heavy chain swinging from his collar, his mouth open in a roar.
must_show: a hulking very dark charcoal-grey orc, darker than every other orc, bare bald head, tusks as long as his face
three big mismatched plates: a black iron breastplate, a steel belly plate, a brown bronze shoulder plate; not a chequer of small squares
an iron collar with one heavy pale steel chain of huge links hanging down the middle of the chest
one huge broad rectangular cleaver in both hands
the most fearsome orc: darker and bigger-tusked than the warlord, and no cloak or helmet
must_not_show: chain wrapped all round the body
only leather straps on the chest
round white disc on the belly
